title: Routine health examination indicators for fatty liver disease risk stratification in adults with thyroid dysfunction: a cross-sectional study of 46,311 individuals

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Routine health examination indicators for fatty liver disease risk stratification in adults with thyroid dysfunction: a cross-sectional study of 46,311 individuals》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p5】From a public health and health management perspective, adults with thyroid dysfunction represent a readily identifiable subgroup for targeted fatty liver risk assessment. These individuals often undergo repeated biochemical monitoring, creating opportunities to integrate liver-metabolic risk stratification into routine follow-up. Because thyroid dysfunction is linked to metabolic alterations that overlap with fatty liver risk, risk stratification within this subgroup may be more clinically actionable than applying a general fatty liver screening approach alone. However, previous studies have mainly focused on associations between thyroid dysfunction and fatty liver disease, while fewer have translated routine health examination data into practical screening-oriented risk stratification tools. Therefore, this large retrospective cross-sectional study of 46,311 adults undergoing routine health examinations had three aims: first, to evaluate the distribution of MAFLD across thyroid function categories; second, to examine the associations of routinely measured thyroid indices, including thyroid-stimulating hormone, free triiodothyronine, and free thyroxine, with MAFLD; and third, to develop and internally validate pragmatic risk stratification models for adults with hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism using routinely available clinical indicators. By reframing thyroid dysfunction as a screening-relevant subgroup within health examination practice, this study seeks to provide evidence for targeted fatty liver risk assessment and post-examination follow-up in real-world health management settings.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Fatty liver disease has become one of the most common chronic liver conditions worldwide and is increasingly recognized as a major public health challenge. Recent global estimates suggest that non-alcoholic fatty liver disease affects approximately one-third of the adult population, with a rising burden driven by obesity, type 2 diabetes, and other cardiometabolic risk factors [1,2]. Because early-stage fatty liver disease is often asymptomatic, many individuals are first identified during routine health examinations rather than through liver-related clinical symptoms. Health examination programs therefore provide an important opportunity for early detection, risk stratification, and timely lifestyle or metabolic intervention. Current clinical guidance also emphasizes case-finding among individuals with cardiometabolic risk factors, abnormal liver enzymes, or radiological evidence of hepatic steatosis [3,4].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Routine health examination indicators for fatty liver disease risk stratification in adults with thyroid dysfunction: a cross-sectional study of 46,311 individuals》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design, setting, and participants · S0002-S2001-p1】This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at the Health Management Center of the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, China. Adults who underwent routine health examinations between November 2019 and February 2025 were screened. Routine examinations included thyroid function testing, biochemical measurements, anthropometric assessment, waist circumference measurement, blood pressure measurement, and abdominal ultrasonography.

【Study design, setting, and participants · S0002-S2001-p2】Individuals were eligible if they were aged 18 years or older and had complete demographic and anthropometric information, thyroid function tests, liver biochemical tests, lipid profiles, fasting plasma glucose, and abdominal ultrasonography required for the study analyses. Participants with one or more of these required data elements missing were excluded, and the final analytic cohort was based on complete cases. Additional study-specific exclusion criteria included pregnancy or lactation; a history of thyroid cancer, thyroidectomy, or radioactive iodine therapy; current or prior use of thyroid hormones or antithyroid drugs; and major liver diseases, including viral hepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, Wilson’s disease, liver malignancy, or previous liver surgery. The liver-related exclusions were applied to reduce etiologic heterogeneity. For individuals with repeated health examination records, only the most recent complete record was retained.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Routine health examination indicators for fatty liver disease risk stratification in adults with thyroid dysfunction: a cross-sectional study of 46,311 individuals》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · S0005-p1】Routine health examination indicators enabled effective fatty liver risk stratification among adults with thyroid dysfunction. These findings support targeted liver-metabolic follow-up in this readily identifiable screening population, although prospective multicenter validation is needed before broader implementation.

【Results · abstract-3-1】Among 46,311 participants, 42,978 were euthyroid, 2,645 had hypothyroidism, and 688 had hyperthyroidism. MAFLD prevalence was 33.0%, 35.5%, and 19.9%, respectively. FT3 was positively associated with MAFLD, whereas FT4 was inversely associated; TSH was not independently associated after full adjustment. The hypothyroid model retained age, BMI, ALT, TG, and HDL-C, with AUCs of 0.906 and 0.901 in the training and validation sets. The hyperthyroid model retained age, BMI, FT4, ALT, and HDL-C, with AUCs of 0.918 and 0.932. Both models showed good calibration and potential utility for post-examination risk stratification.
